Millbrook council approves solar farm

The Millbrook town council voted five to two on Thursday night to approve a 40‑acre solar farm on the former Henley dairy property, ending a debate that has run for most of the year.

Supporters said the project would cut electricity costs for the school district and bring roughly 30 construction jobs to the area. Council member Ana Ruiz called it "the most practical step this town has taken on energy in a decade."

Opponents, including several neighbors along Route 9, argued that the panels would spoil the view from the river​walk and questioned whether the developer had done enough to protect the wetland on the property's eastern edge.

  • Construction is expected to begin in the spring.
  • The farm should produce enough power for about 6,000 homes.

The developer, Bright Acre Energy, said it would plant pollinator meadows beneath the panels and fund a new trail along the river. A final site plan still needs approval from the state environmental board, which is expected to review it in January.

Mayor Lin Park said she understood the concerns but believed the town could not afford to wait. "Every year we delay, our residents pay more," she said after the vote.
